every: Wash with warm water and a stiff brush. A little dish soap is fine.
Scrape stuck food, or scrub with coarse salt and a little water.
Rub a thin coat of oil over the whole surface.
Store it dry. No soaking, no dishwasher.
season: Rub a very thin coat of oil all over, inside and out; wipe off the extra.
Foil on the lower rack; pan upside down on the middle rack.
Bake 1 hour: Lodge says 450–500°F; some extension services use 350°F with 3 to 4 coats.
Turn off the oven and let it cool inside.
rust: Scrub the rust off with steel wool.
Oil it thinly; bake upside down at 450–500°F for 1 hour if the rust was heavy.
remember: Acidic foods (tomato, citrus, wine): under about 45 minutes in bare cast iron. Use enamel or stainless for long simmers.
Enameled cast iron needs no seasoning; don’t heat it empty, and use wood or silicone tools.
Handles get hot. Use an oven mitt every time.
